A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same CAF-7M and DoubleCast study. All 39 pages of v3 and 42 pages of v4, including Appendices A–F, support comparison. Text extraction and visual inspection establish correspondence across relocated figures, tables, and appendix sections.

before.justification: V3 reports original forecasting experiments on CAF-7M, CGTSF, and GIFT-Eval, together with context ablations, scaling studies, and dataset-verification analyses.

after.justification: V4 retains those experiments and adds Time-MMD results, additional baseline evaluations, human context-quality judgments, and training-filtering and verifier-choice studies.

M1.justification: The context-generation, semantic-checking, and CRPS-based verification pipeline is retained, as is DoubleCast’s Chronos backbone, Qwen3-14B encoder, DualT5 attention, and training objective. The new filtering and human-evaluation studies assess the existing procedure rather than introduce replacement components.

E1.justification: V4 adds actual evaluation on Time-MMD across nine domains, substantially broadening external data coverage beyond the retained CGTSF and GIFT-Eval evaluations. Time-MMD appeared in v3 as related work, without the forecasting experiments now reported in Appendix F.3.

E2.justification: Appendix F.4 adds CAF-7M comparisons with Aurora, Chronos-2, FlowState, TimeMixer++, and LLM4TS (Multi-Patch). Table 7 includes Informer in the new Time-MMD comparison. Appendix F.6 additionally compares GPT-5.2 verification against Deepseek V3.2, Claude Sonnet 4.6, and Gemini 2.5 Flash. Comparator membership in Tables 2–3 is retained.

E3.justification: New protocols include filtered-versus-unfiltered training at 5k–50k example budgets for roughly 40k steps, an 11-annotator assessment of 30 contexts, and alternative-verifier testing on 200 HARD windows. Time-MMD adds domain-level MAE evaluation. These additions do not replace the original splits or the 400,000-step DoubleCast training recipe.

E4.justification: V4 adds direct tests of filtering’s sample-efficiency benefit, human judgments of context clarity and plausibility, sensitivity to verifier choice, and Aurora’s sensitivity to shuffled context. These materially expand validation of the data-construction approach. The EASY ablations, scaling studies, filtering-distribution checks, and qualitative forecast examples already existed in v3.

E5.justification: The existing standard errors across windows, fixed random seed 42, and 25 independently sampled Direct Prompt forecasts per instance are retained. The added studies report point estimates and agreement rates without introducing new repeated-run uncertainty, confidence intervals, or significance-testing procedures.

E6.justification: Tables 2–3 and the retained forecasting plots keep their results. V4 adds substantial new entries: filtered/unfiltered validation losses, human judgments, Time-MMD domain MAEs, additional baseline CRPS values, and verifier agreements. Examples include Chronos-2’s ALL CRPS of 0.262 and Aurora’s 0.589 versus 0.643 with shuffled context. These are newly reported comparisons, not revisions of DoubleCast’s existing scores.

T1.justification: Equations 1–19 retain their mathematical content, including context usefulness, DualT5 updates, and metric definitions. V4 corrects the verification passage’s reference from Equation 1 to Equation 2, but introduces no substantive mathematical revision or new proof.

C1.justification: The abstract narrows dataset quality from the primary bottleneck rather than architecture to a major contributing bottleneck. The introduction replaces a guarantee of provably useful context with empirical usefulness under the chosen verifier. The central contributions—CAF-7M, its construction procedure, and demonstrated context utilization and transfer—remain intact.

C2.justification: V4 explicitly limits future-conditioned synthetic contexts to probing context-use capability rather than estimating deployment gains. It adds interpretations of verifier-dependent acceptance, the training quantity–quality trade-off, possible noise-driven scaling saturation, and Time-MMD’s dependence on adaptation and backbone strength. These substantially refine applicability and the interpretation of the evidence.

D1.justification: V4 adds an explicit model-weights access link in Footnote 2, supplementing the existing code and dataset links. It documents budgets and procedures for the new validation studies. The architecture, optimizer, hardware, prompts, and inference details in the existing technical appendices are otherwise retained.

R1.justification: V4 identifies Aurora as the closest concurrent work and positions forecasting-based verification as complementary to its multimodal pretraining approach. It adds references for the newly evaluated methods. Most other bibliography changes update metadata or consolidate duplicate Time-MMD entries; the broader related-work structure remains unchanged.

P1.justification: V4 makes targeted revisions to the abstract, introduction, explanations, and conclusion, adds a conflict-of-interest disclosure, and updates author affiliations, equal-contribution information, and correspondence details. Appendix F gains subsections, but the main narrative order and most existing technical prose are preserved.

P2.justification: V4 adds Tables 5–9 and the two-panel verifier-agreement heatmap in Figure 30. The EASY ablation moves from v3 Figure 23 to v4 Figure 4, with a revised caption. Existing plots and diagrams are retained, while boxed introductory material is simplified and surrounding content is repaginated.

improvement.justification: V4 improves credibility by qualifying v3’s broad guarantees and adding direct evidence about verifier sensitivity, filtering quality, and external transfer. The ecological-validity discussion also makes the scope clearer. The gain is limited by sparse Time-MMD protocol documentation and the unexplained 82% positive majority-vote result over 30 examples in Table 6. The net effect is a better-supported, more carefully bounded paper, with remaining weaknesses in the new evidence.
